statusDetail: Coverage complete across 58 atomic checks. Representative mobile commerce templates, account entry, add-to-cart, and error recovery were exercised; payment completion, authenticated account management, desktop-only mega-menu states, and every category/product variant were not covered because they are repetitive, require credentials, or risk a real transaction.

page.notes: Public Persian RTL marketplace. Rendered content is client-side despite Next.js; a manifest and service worker are present.

paths.description: Homepage and global navigation, representing merchandising, discovery, and site-wide chrome.
Mobile-phone category listing, representing category navigation and product discovery. One category template was sampled because sibling categories share the same shell.
Representative product detail and add-to-cart interaction, covering product information and the primary commercial action.
Search results for گوشی, representing query results, filtering, and dynamic list rendering.
Authentication entry and invalid-empty submission, representing account input and error recovery. No credentials were entered.
Intentional missing URL, representing HTTP/not-found recovery.

findings.summary: The interface ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The product screenshot captured under prefers-color-scheme: dark is byte-identical to the light capture and remains a white surface; CSS probing found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven surface, text, border, icon, and form colors using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Loading motion continues unchanged when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found the same 57 running 1.2-second loading animations as the default condition, despite matchMedia reporting reduce=true.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove looping decorative/loading motion or replace it with a static or low-motion state.

findings.summary: A promotion obscures the homepage immediately on load.
findings.evidence: The first mobile homepage capture is covered by a centered promotional panel and full-page gray scrim before any interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not show the promotion on initial load. Place the offer in-page or defer it until an explicit, relevant action, with a clear light-dismiss path.

findings.summary: The blocking promotion is not exposed as a semantic dialog.
findings.evidence: The screenshot shows a modal interaction, while DOM probes across the audited templates found zero dialog elements, popovers, or role=dialog/aria-modal nodes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog for a genuinely modal flow, including focus management and platform dismissal; use popover for non-modal transient content.

findings.summary: Persistent and promotional chrome competes with core content on mobile.
findings.evidence: The homepage viewport combines a sticky promotional strip, search/address header, floating support control, modal/scrim, and fixed five-item bottom navigation, leaving little primary content visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or collapse nonessential persistent chrome, reserve fixed UI for primary navigation, and keep support/promotion affordances unobtrusive.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is entirely viewport-driven rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: CSS probes across homepage, listing, product, and search found no @container rules, although the same cards and navigation components appear in multiple contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable cards, filters, and navigation components so they respond to available component space, with viewport rules retained for page-level composition.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on sampled interactive controls.
findings.evidence: Programmatic focus on the visible support control and a product link produced outline:none and no box shadow; Lighthouse also found inaccessible interactive elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator on every interactive element and verify the complete keyboard focus walk.

findings.summary: The sampled add-to-cart action did not progress the primary flow.
findings.evidence: The add-to-cart button was activated on the product page, but the post-interaction screenshot is byte-identical to the pre-interaction state and the URL remained on the product page.
findings.suggestedFix: Make add-to-cart reliably update cart state and expose an immediate route or control to review the cart; handle inventory/session failures inline.

findings.summary: Add-to-cart provides no observable success or error feedback in the sampled state.
findings.evidence: After activation there was no dialog, toast, URL change, or visual delta, so the user cannot tell whether the request succeeded or failed.
findings.suggestedFix: Announce success or failure with a persistent, accessible status message and expose retry/review-cart actions without losing product context.

findings.summary: Laboratory loading performance is far outside good Core Web Vitals ranges.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 31.2s, TBT 780ms, and performance 0.46; product LCP was 18.7s with TBT 640ms and performance 0.45.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, shorten dependency chains, server-render meaningful content, and reduce initial JavaScript before tuning secondary work.

findings.summary: Search results undergo a severe late layout shift.
findings.evidence: The mobile search layout observer recorded CLS 0.822, including a single 0.821 shift around 4.5 seconds; other sampled templates stayed near 0.004 or below.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for search controls/results and all late-loaded media, and ensure hydrated/loading states use the final geometry.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting blocks the main thread during load.
findings.evidence: The trace found five long tasks, a longest task of 1,503ms, and 1,567ms total blocking time; Lighthouse reported 5.4s main-thread work and 2.4s JavaScript execution.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long tasks into prioritized chunks, defer noncritical features, and move suitable computation off the main thread.

findings.summary: The initial network dependency graph is oversized and delays critical content.
findings.evidence: The HAR captured 308 requests and 6.47MB transferred; Lighthouse found render-blocking work, weak cache lifetimes, LCP discovery failures, and up to 1.69s render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the critical request chain, preload only the confirmed LCP dependency, improve cache lifetimes, and defer noncritical fonts/scripts/styles.

findings.summary: The page ships a large amount of unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 186 script requests transferring 4.29MB; Lighthouse estimated 1.73MB unused JavaScript on home and 1.88MB on product, plus about 101KB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Measure route-level coverage, split bundles by feature/template, remove duplicate/legacy dependencies, and load analytics and optional widgets only when needed.

findings.summary: Some links and buttons lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-name on the homepage and both button-name and link-name on the product page; the DOM probe counted empty links and images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every interactive element a stable accessible name, add meaningful alt text, and expose decorative images with empty alt only when intentional.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the color-contrast audit on both homepage and product templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust failing foreground/background tokens to WCAG contrast thresholds and test normal, dark, disabled, hover, focus, and forced-color states.

findings.summary: Heading structure and visible keyboard focus are unreliable.
findings.evidence: The product heading sequence jumps from H2 to H4 and Lighthouse failed heading-order; focused sampled controls had no visible outline or shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sequential heading hierarchy and add consistent :focus-visible treatment while preserving logical DOM/tab order.

findings.summary: The viewport declaration prevents normal user zoom.
findings.evidence: All sampled pages declare maximum-scale=1.0; Lighthouse failed meta-viewport because the maximum scale is below 5.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and any user-scalable restriction, then verify reflow and fixed controls at 200% and 400% zoom.

findings.summary: Many image elements omit intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The DOM probes found 16 of 30 homepage images and 3 of 7 product images missing width or height attributes; the image primitive also found four of five initially loaded images missing dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide width and height or an equivalent reserved aspect-ratio for every content image, including lazy and dynamically inserted media.

findings.summary: Large first-party bundles lack source maps and the page reports browser inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript, cookie-related DevTools issues, and a BFCache blocker caused by an open WebSocket.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish production source maps to the error/debugging pipeline, resolve cookie warnings, and close or suspend WebSockets when pages enter the background/pagehide lifecycle.

findings.summary: Product and homepage entities lack structured and social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: DOM probes found no JSON-LD and no Open Graph metadata on the homepage or representative product, despite the product having a clearly identifiable name, price, image, and rating.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Product/Offer and Organization JSON-LD plus Open Graph/Twitter metadata that matches visible content.

findings.summary: Important browser security headers and cookie protections are missing.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but the response has no CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; the cookie audit found 10 insecure cookies and pervasive SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and secure cookie defaults; scope SameSite=None only to cookies that truly require cross-site use.

findings.summary: The initial page load has a broad tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe observed 16 non-page origins, Google Tag Manager/Analytics, InTrack, Digiwise, Yektanet and MediaAd endpoints; Lighthouse found third-party cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors and identifiers, gate optional analytics behind consent, batch first-party analytics, and load nonessential third parties only after relevant interaction.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Neither CSP frame-ancestors nor X-Frame-Options is present, and Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and X-Content-Type-Options are absent; cookies include long-lived tracking identifiers.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options as a compatibility layer), nosniff, strict referrer and permissions policies, and review long-lived identifier cookies.

findings.summary: Core content is unavailable without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability captures for home, product, and search report 0% content coverage and only 26 raw text characters; the product raw response does not contain its title or H1, while the rendered page has full product content.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render core navigation, listing, and product content into the initial HTML and layer interactivity on top with hydration/progressive enhancement.

findings.summary: The installable shell has no offline content fallback.
findings.evidence: A valid manifest and active service worker exist, but Cache Storage is empty and sw9.js only handles analytics rewriting/push imports; it defines no navigation cache or offline fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a small, versioned offline navigation fallback and cache only essential shell/recovery assets, while keeping commerce data network-first and visibly stale-safe.

findings.summary: The sign-in identifier field explicitly disables autocomplete.
findings.evidence: The login probe found the labelled username field uses autocomplete="off", preventing password managers and browser autofill from assisting with the email/mobile identifier.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the appropriate autocomplete token (username, email, or tel as the flow permits) and allow password-manager/autofill assistance.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes substantial bytes.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 817KB image-delivery savings on the homepage; the image primitive found a legacy GIF, missing responsive sources, and oversized delivery signals.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace animated/decorative GIFs with efficient formats, serve responsive AVIF/WebP sources, and size each image to its rendered slot.

findings.summary: The initial experience performs disproportionate network and JavaScript work.
findings.evidence: The homepage initiated 308 requests, 186 scripts, 28 XHR/fetches, 57 simultaneous animations, and a 1.5-second main-thread task before meaningful completion.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay background data, analytics, recommendations, and motion until idle or user intent; cancel work when hidden and consolidate requests.

findings.summary: Third-party and script weight is not proportionate to the first mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: The HAR transferred 6.47MB, including 4.29MB of scripts and 1.39MB of images, while the tracker probe observed 16 external origins and the first viewport was still dominated by promotion/chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Set route-specific budgets for transfer size, JavaScript, images, fonts, and external origins; remove vendors and defer media that does not support the first task.

findings.summary: The commerce surface exposes no structured agent capabilities.
findings.evidence: No WebMCP/agent-tool registration was found, product content is absent from raw HTML, Lighthouse agentic-browsing scored 0.33, and /llms.txt returned the application shell rather than agent guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: After fixing server-rendered content, expose narrowly scoped, confirmable product-search/cart capabilities through emerging agent interfaces; never allow silent purchasing.

findings.summary: The homepage starts with a heavy memory and DOM footprint.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contained 916,850 heap-snapshot nodes and 91.7MB self size; the live probe found about 6,251 DOM elements and 52.3MB used JS heap before repeated scrolling.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce hydrated DOM and initial feature modules, virtualize long merchandising sections, and remove unnecessary closures/observers from the initial route.

taskList.title: Server-render core home, listing, search, and product content
Cut LCP, initial JavaScript, main-thread work, and dependency depth
Deploy CSP and complete security/cookie browser policies
Remove or defer initial trackers and enforce third-party budgets
Fix unnamed controls, heading order, contrast, focus, and zoom
Remove the load-time promo modal or rebuild it with a semantic primitive
Make add-to-cart progress and feedback unambiguous
Optimize responsive image delivery and remove legacy GIF cost

checkOutcomes.evidence: Both conditions retained 57 running loading animations.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Text, breadcrumb links, price, rating, and purchase control remain visible with system colors.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Rendered styles contain view-transition rules across all four representative templates.

checkOutcomes.method: Visual recon and CSS feature probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No scrollytelling, parallax, or scroll-linked animation surface was present on the sampled commerce templates; no animation-timeline rule was found.
checkOutcomes.reason: No scroll-linked motion existed to implement declaratively.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The mobile merchandising/gallery surfaces use native scrolling with scroll-snap rules and do not expose a custom pointer-driven gesture requirement.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Product section navigation and the purchase action remain persistently available while the page scrolls to y=1200.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected active mobile flows and overlay primitives.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No tooltip, popover, or edge-positioned menu was invoked in the representative mobile journeys; the observed promotion is viewport-modal rather than anchor-attached.
checkOutcomes.reason: No anchor-attached overlay applied to the exercised paths.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile screenshot and navigation-state inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Breadcrumbs, selected bottom-navigation state, search query, result count, and sticky purchase action clearly preserve location and next action.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Visible modal behavior has no dialog, popover, role=dialog, or aria-modal representation.

checkOutcomes.method: First-viewport visual hierarchy and fixed-element probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Promotion, support, sticky header, and bottom navigation consume most of the mobile viewport.

checkOutcomes.method: Layout metrics at 360x800 across four templates.
checkOutcomes.evidence: All four paths reported scrollWidth=clientWidth=360 and zero horizontal overflow.

checkOutcomes.method: Cross-template stylesheet feature probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No @container rules were found for reused commerce components.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected first viewports and heading/action hierarchy.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared add-to-cart, invalid-login, and 404 recovery states.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse on home/product plus DevTools trace.

checkOutcomes.method: Trace long-task analysis and Lighthouse diagnostics.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM anchor/viewport probes and Lighthouse SEO.

checkOutcomes.method: Header, cookie, HTTPS, and secret scans.
checkOutcomes.evidence: HTTPS/HSTS pass and no secrets were found, but CSP/nosniff and secure cookie defaults fail.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR and tracker-origin inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Sixteen external origins and multiple analytics/identity vendors load on the initial route.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse permission-timing audits and live OIDC login inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No geolocation/notification prompt occurred on load; login redirects through OIDC with PKCE and starts with an email/mobile identifier rather than a page-embedded password form.

checkOutcomes.method: Security header and cookie-policy inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Clickjacking, MIME, referrer, permissions, and cookie defenses are incomplete.

checkOutcomes.method: Raw HTML versus rendered DOM discoverability comparison.

checkOutcomes.method: Representative mobile visual states, forced colors, and repeated scrolling.

checkOutcomes.method: Manifest/service-worker/cache inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The site is installable, but the service worker has no offline navigation fallback and Cache Storage is empty.

checkOutcomes.method: Loaded an intentional missing URL and inspected recovery.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The not-found page clearly states the page is missing and provides a homepage recovery link.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM language/direction and CSS logical-property inspection.

checkOutcomes.method: Visual inspection of locale-sensitive prices, counts, and ratings.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon of representative commerce templates and data types.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The sampled homepage, listing, product, search, login, and error paths expose no event schedules, user times, recurring intervals, or time-zone-sensitive values.
checkOutcomes.reason: No time-zone-sensitive user data appeared in the audited scope.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected promotion, product pricing, login terms, and recovery states.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Promotion dismissal uses neutral wording; product price/action and login terms are visible, with no preselected paid option or confirmshaming observed.

checkOutcomes.method: Submitted the login form empty and inspected error announcement.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected product pricing/action and OIDC account entry.

checkOutcomes.method: Image primitive, HAR, and Lighthouse image-delivery insight.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR request mix, trace, and animation activity inspection.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR byte/origin budget and first-viewport visual inspection.

checkOutcomes.method: Baseline/post heap summaries and ten repeated bottom/top scroll cycles.
